Question
What should my business automate first?

Choose one repeated job with a clear input, finished output and a person who can check the result. Measure the current process, run a small test and include review time in the comparison.

Read the full explanation

Question
What makes a task a good candidate for AI?

Look for repetition, usable examples, accessible inputs and a checkable result. A defined owner and a clear purpose for the time recovered make the first project easier to evaluate.

Question
How do I measure the starting point before an AI project?

Use recent work to record task frequency, total handling time and common corrections. Name the person who decides whether the new output is acceptable.

BUSINESS AI
Question
Why is automating an entire department a difficult first project?

A department contains many different inputs, decisions and exceptions. Narrow the scope to one piece of work so you can define completion and test the result.

Read the full explanation
Explore answer
↗
BUSINESS AI
Question
Do I need to replace my existing software to use AI?

Start by mapping the work between your current tools. Whether an integration is useful depends on what those tools can connect to and what the workflow needs.

Explore answer

BUSINESS AI
Question
How do I decide whether an AI test was successful?

Compare quality and total work, including preparation, review and correction. Look for useful results across ordinary and awkward inputs before expanding the scope.

Read the full explanation

BUSINESS AI
Question
Are hours saved by AI the same as money saved?

Hours freed create capacity. The business result depends on how that capacity is used, such as clearing a backlog, responding sooner or giving specialists time for higher-value work.

Read the full explanation
Explore answer

Question
Who should own an AI workflow?

Name the person responsible for checking the output, handling exceptions and maintaining the instructions. Ownership should be clear before the workflow expands.
